name: Chioggia
title: Chioggia Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Small Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Chioggia for small cargo ships, steel fishing vessels, tugs and lagoon workboats: hull, hold, deck and tank steel readings.
h1: Ship Steel Condition Surveys in Chioggia, Southern Venice Lagoon
intro: Chioggia lies at the southern end of the Venice lagoon and works as a fishing port, a small cargo harbour and a base for lagoon craft. Steel fishing vessels, coasters, tugs and workboats are the usual customers for thickness gauging, often for an insurer, a buyer or a repair decision. Atlantis NDT sends technicians from India to the vessel, with nobody based on the Veneto coast, and fits the work around the tide, the fish market cycle and the cargo stop.

highlights.p: Chioggia is home to a large Adriatic fishing fleet, so steel trawlers and other fishing boats make up much of the ship stock, and owners ask for hull plating records for insurers, buyers and repair planning.

highlights.h: Small cargo ships at the quays
highlights.p: Coasters and small bulk and general cargo ships call at the commercial quays, where a cargo stop gives enough time to gauge holds, hatch covers and an accessible ballast tank group.

Small yards in and around the town service lagoon craft, and the inlet barrier with its navigation lock affects ship movements, so gauging is planned around the ship's arrival rather than a fixed hour.

port.h: The port of Chioggia: inlet, fish market quays and the commercial wharves
p: Chioggia sits at the southern end of the Venice lagoon, on an island joined to the mainland by bridges, with the beach resort of Sottomarina on the seaward side. Ships reach the harbour through the Chioggia inlet, one of the three openings between the lagoon and the Adriatic, where mobile barriers and a navigation lock now stand alongside the breakwaters. The town is built around a main canal lined with fishing boats, while the commercial quays and a marina occupy separate parts of the water. Depth in the approach limits the size of the ships that can enter, and lagoon channels need careful pilotage.

The port's best-known role is fishing. Chioggia has long been one of the main fishing centres of the northern Adriatic, with trawlers, fishing boats and a large fish market, and boats work in rhythm with the catch and the market, leaving at night and returning in the morning. Commercial traffic is smaller but real: coasters and small bulk and general cargo ships bring and take cereals, fertiliser, steel and other goods, and the port forms part of the northern Adriatic port system together with Venice, which sits a few miles to the north.

These ships present a particular profile for gauging. Steel fishing vessels operate in salt water for long hours and are often old, with corrosion in the bilges, around the fish hold and in the engine room structure. Small cargo ships show wear in hold frames and the underside of hatch covers. Tugs and workboats that serve the lagoon accumulate damage from fenders and pushing work. Many of these vessels are not under full class supervision, so independent thickness records carry weight with insurers and buyers, and a short, well-organised survey can answer most of their questions.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Chioggia: quays, lay-by berths and the lagoon yards
p: Gauging on small cargo ships takes place alongside at the commercial quays during or after cargo operations, with holds measured once empty and safe for entry. Because the ships are small, a team can often cover holds, deck, hatch covers and an accessible group of ballast tanks in a single day. For fishing vessels, the best time is when the boat is tied up in the canal between trips or laid up for the closed season, with the crew preparing the bilges and the hold areas beforehand so that the plating is clean enough for readings.

Lagoon yards in and around the town can lift or slip small hulls, which gives access to the bottom plating of fishing boats, tugs and workboats. These yards do not take large merchant ships, so a coaster needing a renewal survey docks elsewhere on the Adriatic, for example at Venice-area yards, Ravenna or on the Croatian coast, and a thickness survey in Chioggia beforehand helps that yard plan steel renewal. Ships waiting for a berth or the tide may anchor off the inlet, where a limited condition check is possible in calm conditions.
list: Commercial quays — hold frames, tank tops, hatch covers and coamings on coasters and small bulk carriers after discharge
Fishing canal berths — hull plating, bilges and fish hold structure of steel fishing vessels tied up between trips
Lagoon yards and slipways — bottom and shell plating of tugs, fishing boats and workboats when hauled out
Lay-by berths — owner's condition checks on ships laid up or awaiting sale or employment
Anchorage off the inlet — limited condition checks on ships waiting for a berth, by launch through the ship's agent

context.h: Port state control and regulation for small ships and fishing craft in Chioggia
p: Port state control applies to foreign-flag cargo ships in Chioggia, exercised by the Italian Coast Guard through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto) under the Paris MoU, and older coasters tend to attract more attention because of their ship risk profile. Fishing vessels fall under separate flag state and fisheries safety rules rather than the Paris MoU, and many are not classed, so thickness records are usually requested by insurers, lenders or buyers rather than by a surveyor. For classed small ships, the society sets which readings each renewal or intermediate survey needs.

Wider rules touch this market in several ways. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships calling at EU ports, and the owners of old coasters who are considering sale or scrapping use gauging records to judge the remaining value of the steel. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime affect cargo ships but not fishing boats, and fleet renewal programmes for fishing vessels, supported by regional funds, can bring a wave of surveys when owners consider replacement or major repair. Environmental protection in the lagoon also limits the scope of cleaning work near the water.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Chioggia
jobs.p: Chioggia jobs are short and specific. A coaster may be alongside for a day, a fishing boat may be in the canal for a weekend, and a tug may be on a slipway for a week. We agree the list of spaces, the surface preparation and the report layout with the owner or superintendent before the technicians travel from India, and the report is arranged location by location so that an insurer, buyer or surveyor can compare it with later readings.
list: Hold frame and hatch cover gauging on a coaster at the commercial quay, ahead of an intermediate survey
Hull plating and bilge readings on a steel fishing vessel tied up in the canal, for an insurer or a prospective buyer
Bottom plating survey of a tug or workboat on a lagoon slipway before repair or a change of ownership
Ballast tank readings on a small general cargo ship, so a repair yard elsewhere on the Adriatic can plan steel renewal
Pre-purchase gauging of a small bulk carrier at a lay-by berth, covering holds, deck and accessible tanks

logistics: Venice Marco Polo Airport is the usual entry point and is connected to Chioggia by road, while Treviso and Bologna offer further options. The ship's agent, or the owner where a vessel has no agent, arranges port access and any launch for anchorage work. Our technicians are Indian nationals travelling on Schengen visas, so we start the application when the job is confirmed and book flights once the ship's schedule or the boat's availability in Chioggia is firm. Combining Chioggia with Venice or Ravenna in one trip often makes sense for the team.

faqs.q: Can a steel fishing boat in Chioggia be gauged for an insurer?
faqs.a: Yes. We measure hull plating, bilges and the fish hold structure at agreed points, record the surface condition at each reading, and produce a short report showing the weakest areas. The crew prepares the locations beforehand, and the report is laid out so an insurer or buyer can compare it with a later survey.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Chioggia for coasters?
faqs.a: Lagoon yards handle small hulls such as fishing boats, tugs and workboats, but a coaster needing a renewal survey usually docks elsewhere on the Adriatic. We gauge the ship in Chioggia first, giving the chosen yard measured steel estimates, then travel to the yard for the full programme if you ask.

faqs.q: Does the inlet barrier affect a gauging job?
faqs.a: It affects the ship's arrival and departure rather than the gauging. When the barriers are raised or the lock is in use, movements can be delayed. We fix flights once the ship's arrival is confirmed, and keep the scope prioritised so the most important spaces are measured first if the window turns out shorter.

faqs.q: Can holds on a small coaster be gauged during discharge?
faqs.a: Only once the hold is empty, cleaned and cleared for entry. During discharge, we can measure the deck and hatch cover structure. After discharge, the team enters the hold and measures frames, bulkheads and the tank top, recording surface condition at each location.

faqs.q: Can gauging in Chioggia be combined with Venice or Ravenna?
faqs.a: Yes, because the ports are close. One mobilisation can cover a ship at Chioggia and another at Venice or Ravenna if the schedules allow. Send the ship itineraries when you enquire, and we will sequence the work so the team is not waiting between calls.
